summary: css-overscroll-contain exfiltrates host environment and runs container-escape probes to webhook.site
details: Package is published as a CSS overscroll-behavior polyfill, but index.js exports an empty object and the real payload is in thunderboltRegistry.js. On load, that file executes an IIFE that shells out via child_process.execSync and Perl to collect host identity (id, uname, pid), file descriptors from /proc/self/fd, mount tables, running processes, and the environment filtered for key/token/secret/pass/auth/host/port/url/endpoint/service/kube substrings, POSTing each result to the hardcoded collector https://webhook.site/4a7272ce-00ca-48b2-904a-05679b11493b. The same IIFE runs active exploitation probes: mknod of CUSE/FUSE device nodes via raw syscall 259, memfd_create+exec via syscall 319, symlink traversal to /proc/1/root, and unshare-based user-namespace mount scans. thunderboltRegistry.js also exports a Proxy that impersonates internal Wix Thunderbolt registry module names (thunderboltRegistry, siteAssetsRegistry, documentManagementRegistry, editorRegistry, corvidRegistry, dataBindingRegistry, and others), and registry-manifest.min.json redirects those names to this file via unpkg — a dependency-confusion/typosquat shape targeting the Wix Thunderbolt build pipeline.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
